expectations.text: Separates externally published findings from this skill's own self-set baselines rather than presenting one undifferentiated list.
expectations.evidence: "Numbers below are split into sourced research — citable as an industry standard — and production baselines — defensible engineering decisions, not something to defend as 'the industry says.' Mixing the two is the fastest way to lose a citation fight with a skeptical VP, so they're kept separate." The document consistently uses 'Sourced, hard data:' headers and a final 'Internal baseline (not externally sourced)' citation entry.

expectations.text: Labels the 24pt terminal and 20pt editor figures as self-set baselines, not an industry standard.
expectations.evidence: "Important for the citation slide: these are NOT an industry standard. They are this skill's own baseline, chosen to survive small-screen playback." Also citation block item 6: "Internal baseline (not externally sourced): code legibility floors — terminal ≥24pt, editor ≥20pt, verified at phone-sized playback."

expectations.text: Attributes the median-engagement and length findings to the large MOOC instructional-video study, including its session count.
expectations.evidence: "Source: Guo, P.J., Kim, J., & Rubin, R. (2014). 'How Video Production Affects Student Engagement: An Empirical Study of MOOC Videos.' ACM Learning@Scale 2014. n = 6,902,358 viewing sessions, 4 edX courses, Fall 2012 — the largest published study of instructional-video engagement to date."

expectations.text: States the finding that median engagement time is at most about six minutes regardless of total video length.
expectations.evidence: "Median engagement time tops out at 6 minutes, regardless of total video length."

expectations.text: States that viewers typically get less than halfway through videos longer than nine minutes.
expectations.evidence: "Viewers 'often make it less than halfway through videos longer than 9 minutes.'"

expectations.text: States the study's own limitations: a retrospective log study rather than an experiment, on a MOOC corpus.
expectations.evidence: "Caveat to state alongside the number: this is a retrospective log study (watch-time proxy, not a controlled experiment), across 4 math/science MOOCs, with self-selected early-adopter learners."

expectations.text: States that watch time is a proxy for engagement and that engagement is not learning.
expectations.evidence: "this is a retrospective log study (watch-time proxy, not a controlled experiment)... Watch time ≠ learning."

expectations.text: Declines to cite the widely circulated 100%/50%/20% engagement table as a finding, or flags it as a secondary rendering of a normalized plot.
expectations.evidence: "Myth to pre-empt: the widely-circulated '100% / 50% / 20% engagement by length' table is a *secondary, simplified rendering* of Guo et al.'s boxplot, not a number the paper itself states."

expectations.text: Attributes the 52% engagement rate for under-one-minute videos to the hosted-video industry report and flags it as a business-video corpus rather than a teaching one.
expectations.evidence: "videos under 1 minute average a 52% engagement rate... Source: Wistia, '2026 State of Video' report, 13M+ hosted videos. This is a business-video corpus, not a teaching one — cite it only as a same-direction cross-check, not primary evidence."

expectations.text: Identifies the 30-second intro window as a measurement boundary defined by the video platform's retention report.
expectations.evidence: "30 seconds is the hard number — but it's a *platform measurement definition*, not a stylistic guideline: the dominant video platform's audience-retention report defines 'intro retention' as the share of viewers still watching after the first 30 seconds."

expectations.text: Attributes the roughly five-second ceremony threshold to a usability finding about perceived intro length rather than to a style rule.
expectations.evidence: "Ceremony budget inside that window: ~5 seconds... Source: Nielsen Norman Group, video usability research — a measured perception threshold, not a hard cutoff. Round it to '~5 seconds' on a slide, not 'exactly 5.'"

expectations.text: Labels the roughly six-minute segment ceiling as this skill's own baseline, applied at the segment level rather than the video level.
expectations.evidence: The transcript instead attributes the 6-minute segmentation guidance directly to the study: "segment any video into chunks under 6 minutes, whatever the total runtime — that's Guo et al.'s own headline recommendation, tested against a real course pair." It is never described as the skill's own self-set baseline; it is presented as sourced research, contradicting this rubric item's requirement.

expectations.text: Warns that presenting a self-set number as an industry standard will fail in a review once someone checks it.
expectations.evidence: "Mixing the two is the fastest way to lose a citation fight with a skeptical VP, so they're kept separate." and "If your VP asks 'who says 24pt,' the honest answer is 'no external source does — we set that floor internally, for phone legibility.' State it that way; don't attribute it to a study that didn't measure it."
